extracted.intended_audience: aspiring essayists, poets, and writers of polite/humorous literature; general readers interested in wit and style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing clear, tasteful, and genuinely witty prose and comedy; distinguishes true wit from various antiquated or contrived 'false wit' practices and gives practical stylistic/process recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity for ordinary capacities
rubrics_metrics.description: Make what you say intelligible to ordinary Capacities; if parts are 'a little out of their Reach', reassure readers and aim to clarify in subsequent pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write so general readers can follow; don't aim at constant obscurity or pedantic obscureness. If a passage is difficult, mitigate by promising clearer exposition later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devote uninterrupted time to treat a subject properly
rubrics_metrics.description: I intend to lay aside a whole Week for this Undertaking, that the Scheme of my Thoughts may not be broken and interrupted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set aside concentrated, uninterrupted work time when treating a large, important subject to preserve coherence and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and cultural purpose: banish vice and ignorance
rubrics_metrics.description: The great and only End of these my Speculations is to banish Vice and Ignorance out of the Territories of Great-Britain; to establish among us a Taste of polite Writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for writing that improves public taste and morals—wit should educate and refine, not merely amuse or shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refinement and perfection of comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Impart notions of Comedy as they may tend to its Refinement and Perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat comedy as an art to be perfected: focus on improving taste, structure, and subtlety rather than crude or coarse humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid antiquated or 'false' wit devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace out the history of false Wit and distinguish several Kinds of it; avoid attempts to revive antiquated modes (acrosticks, shaped poems, odd conceits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't revive gimmicky antiquarian forms simply for novelty; these modes often substitute mechanical cleverness for substantive sense or beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sacrifice sense to shape (avoid 'picture' poems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some poets fashioned poems into shapes (egg, wings, axe, altar) and cramped or stretched verse to fit the figure—prioritising shape over sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid forcing meter, diction, or meaning to fit an external shape; tortured phrasing and contrivance are anti-patterns (Procrustes analogy: stretching/chopping lines to fit a mould).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid lipogrammatic feats (letter-dropping) as literary vanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Lipogrammiatists omit particular letters from whole poems (e.g., Tryphiodorus' books excluding letters); this yields unnatural phrasing and a treasury of obsolete or barbarous words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constraints that ban common letters/words produce awkward constructions and encourage obsolete or forced diction—poor foundation for genuine wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rebuses/pictorial substitutions as poor conceits
rubrics_metrics.description: Substituting pictures for words (rebus) can be a conceit; while sometimes historical/necessary, in many contexts it appears as low punning or a poor taste (e.g., sculptural devices on Blenheim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuses may be witty in trivial contexts but are inappropriate in serious works or grand design—they risk reducing dignity to a pun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the echo-device that supplies answers and rhymes
rubrics_metrics.description: Making an Echo give rational answers or supply rhymes (as in some Ovidian/Erasmian conceits and Hudibras' ridicule) leads to absurd and unconvincing dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on contrived devices (an echo that 'helps out' the poet) to manufacture wit or complete verses—it invites ridicule and undermines authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: True wit should be natural, not mere industrious contrivance
rubrics_metrics.description: Pedants who lack genius may produce 'elaborate trifles' by immense labour; better be a galley-slave than to be a wit earned only by painful contrivance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer spontaneity, genuine insight, and natural talent over laborious, artificial cleverness; avoid showing off learned tricks that mask lack of true imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match style/register to subject (avoid groveling style for the sublime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in a manner suitable to the subject so as not to be censured for composing on the sublime 'in a low groveling Stile.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust diction and tone to the gravity or loftiness of the subject—misregister (too lowly a style for high topics) is a fault.
